name: Ductal carcinoma in situ
theme: recurrence is not survival · the watching frontier

meta.title: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Ductal carcinoma in situ (stage 0 breast cancer), adult
meta.population: Adults with pure DCIS - roughly one in four or five screen-detected breast cancers, and the registry's clearest case of a disease where the treatment decision is NOT about survival: 20-year breast-cancer mortality is 3.3% essentially regardless of local-therapy intensity (Narod, SEER n=108,196). Every choice on this menu - watching included - renders the same survival number, because that is the evidence; the real decision currencies are recurrence risk, treatment burden, and peace of mind. Microinvasion (T1mi) is INVASIVE disease and exits to the live early-stage trainer; LCIS is a risk marker, not cancer, and exits to risk-reduction counseling; Paget of the nipple follows its underlying lesion.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the diagnosis where de-escalation questions outnumber escalation questions and the survival scoreboard is DELIBERATELY, PERFECTLY FLAT (property-enforced): lumpectomy+RT, excision alone, mastectomy, and active monitoring all display the Narod-anchored ~97/100 twenty-year breast-cancer-specific survival, because no randomized or population evidence separates them on survival - radiotherapy halves recurrence (B-17, RTOG 9804) without moving mortality, endocrine therapy trims recurrence (B-24, B-35) without moving mortality, and COMET just showed active m…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: AJCC 8th edition: Tis (DCIS); LCIS removed from staging (benign entity); T1mi (<=1 mm) classifies as invasive T1
meta.response: Not applicable in the classic sense - the decision instruments are pathology (grade, extent, margins), receptor status, and time; COMET made 2-year invasive-cancer rate the frontier's endpoint

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: DCIS is a screening-era diagnosis (the slider starts at 40 with the mammograms). Narod's honest asterisk: diagnosis under 35 carries higher mortality (7.8%) - rare, and worth knowing the flat theorem…
Patient.helpPatient: This diagnosis usually arrives with routine mammograms - and at almost every age, the survival news is already excellent.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Almost always 0 in a screen-detected stage-0 diagnosis - when it is not, competing health priorities strengthen the de-escalation options honestly.

Disease.label: Pathology (the three-way read)
Disease.help: One millimeter decides a pathway: any microinvasion makes this invasive breast cancer (AJCC T1mi) with full staging and the live early-stage trainer's menu; pure LCIS goes the other direction entirel…
Disease.helpPatient: The pathologist's fine print sorts this into one of three very different situations - two of them leave this page.

Disease.label: Nuclear grade
Disease.help: The recurrence ledger's biggest lever (E5194 - a non-randomized cohort, said plainly): high grade nearly doubles events after excision alone and closes the monitoring option. It moves recurrence fore…

Disease.help: HR+ disease gets two extra tools: endocrine recurrence-trimming (B-24 tamoxifen; B-35 anastrozole) and the active-monitoring option (COMET required HR+). Neither tool has ever moved survival - the ca…
Disease.helpPatient: A hormone-sensitive result opens a preventive tablet option and, for the lowest-risk lesions, the option of careful watching.

Disease.help: Extent is a feasibility input, not a danger input: extensive disease makes clean-margin conservation impossible, so mastectomy leads - and even then the survival number does not move, which the maste…

Newly diagnosed.name: Lumpectomy + radiotherapy (recurrence halved; survival untouched)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (B-17, RTOG 9804) - recurrence endpoints
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: surgical recovery plus a short modern RT course; the trade is weeks of treatment for a halved recurrence ledger
Newly diagnosed.patient: Remove the lesion, add short radiation: the return-risk is halved - and the survival number was already excellent before either step.

Newly diagnosed.name: Excision alone (good-risk lesions; endocrine can trim the rest)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: prospective cohorts (E5194) + the randomized observation arm (RTOG 9804)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: one operation; the ongoing cost is a higher-but-survival-neutral recurrence forecast and the vigilance that rides with it
Newly diagnosed.patient: Remove the lesion and stop: for calm-looking, well-cleared lesions, decades of study back this - with a somewhat higher chance of dealing with a return, and the same survival.

Newly diagnosed.name: Mastectomy (extent or preference; the same survival line)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: surgical standard for extent; no randomized survival comparison exists or is needed - the population data answer it
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the largest operation on the menu, chosen exactly when its certainty is worth that - the card refuses to imply a survival return on it
Newly diagnosed.patient: Removing the breast nearly eliminates the chance of a return there - and it is an honest card: it does not add survival, because survival was not the problem.

Newly diagnosed.name: Active monitoring (COMET - the frontier, honestly young)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: trial-established option for low-risk HR+ disease (guideline uptake evolving - secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized noninferiority - 2-YEAR endpoint (young; longer follow-up pending)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: no treatment toxicity at all; the honest costs are surveillance cadence and living with a monitored lesion - which COMET measured and found QoL-neutral at 2 ye…
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the lowest-risk lesions: watching closely instead of operating - the randomized trial found no excess invasive cancer at two years and no cost in worry or quality of life. Honest label: two years is early, and the longer answers are coming.
drugs: Active monitoring program (6-monthly imaging; endocrine therapy optional)

Newly diagnosed.name: Decline intervention and surveillance
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.evidence: teaching estimate (flagged) anchored to the population mortality data
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none; the accepted cost is discovering any progression late rather than early
Newly diagnosed.patient: Even declining everything, the survival outlook remains very good - what is given up is the early-warning system, and the card says exactly that.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Recurrence salvage (DCIS-again: operate; invasive: a different trainer's case)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: usually mastectomy after a conserved-breast recurrence; the invasive branch adds the invasive world's decisions
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If it returns, the first question is what returned: the same stage-0 finding is operated on again with the same excellent outlook; an invasive return moves to the invasive trainer's proven playbook.
drugs: Re-excision or mastectomy per biology and prior therapy

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Decline salvage
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: none; the accepted cost is not knowing which branch of the fork this recurrence took
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Declining again is still survivable-by-the-numbers - the one strong recommendation the card keeps is the biopsy, so the choice is made knowing which situation this is.

refs.label: Narod et al. Breast cancer mortality after a diagnosis of DCIS (SEER, n=108,196): 20-yr breast-cancer-specific mortality 3.3% - RT reduced recurrence but NOT mortality (0.8% vs 0.9%); 517 fatal cases had no prior in-breast invasive recurrence; age <35 (7.8%) and Black women (7.0%) carry the theorem's honest edges. JAMA Oncol 2015;1:888-96

Wapnir et al. NSABP B-17/B-24 long-term (median ~17 yr): RT halved invasive in-breast recurrence (HR 0.48; 15-yr 8.9% vs 19.4%); tamoxifen cut it further (HR 0.68) - and 15-yr breast-cancer death stayed 2-5% in every arm. Recurrence tools, not survival tools. JNCI 2011;103:478-88
Wapnir et al. (same long-term report) - the recurrence-fork evidence base: invasive vs DCIS ipsilateral events tracked over decades. JNCI 2011;103:478-88

McCormick et al. RTOG 9804 15-yr (good-risk DCIS, randomized RT vs observation): ipsilateral recurrence 7.1% vs 15.1% (HR 0.36) - and the authors' own conclusion, rendered verbatim on the card: 'not an absolute indication... should inform shared decisions.' (Don't mix with the 2015 paper's 7-yr 0.9%/6.7%.) JCO 2021;39:3574-82

Solin et al. ECOG-ACRIN E5194 (excision alone, prospective NON-RANDOMIZED cohorts, margins >=3 mm): 12-yr ipsilateral events 14.4% (low/int grade <=2.5 cm) vs 24.6% (high grade <=1 cm); risk rises without plateau. JCO 2015;33:3938-44

Wright et al. Combined RTOG 9804 + E5194 analysis (2026): in good-risk DCIS managed with lumpectomy alone, tamoxifen cut 15-yr recurrence to 11.4% from 19.0% (HR 0.54) - the fresh evidence for the excision-plus-endocrine road. IJROBP 2026

Margolese et al. NSABP B-35 (postmenopausal HR+ DCIS after BCS+RT): anastrozole vs tamoxifen - breast-cancer-free-interval HR 0.73 (p=0.023), benefit confined to age <60; the Ganz QoL companion mapped the trade (vasomotor vs musculoskeletal). Cite as Lancet 2016;387:849-56 (epub Dec 2015 - the year trap, avoided)

Hwang et al. COMET randomized trial (active monitoring vs guideline care, low-risk HR+ grade 1-2 DCIS, n=957): 2-yr ipsilateral invasive cancer 4.2% vs 5.9% - NONINFERIOR (upper CI 0.95% vs 5% bound); 82/484 monitored patients had surgery anyway; 5/7-yr endpoints pending ~2030. Cite as JAMA 2025;333:972-80 (Dec-2024 readout - the year trap, avoided)

Partridge et al. COMET quality-of-life companion: QoL, anxiety, depression, and symptoms indistinguishable between monitoring and surgery over 2 years - watching did not cost peace of mind. JAMA Oncol 2025;11:300-9

Solin et al. Oncotype DCIS score validation (E5194 tissue, n=327): 10-yr ipsilateral events 10.6%/26.7%/25.9% by score group - prognostically validated; NO randomized proof of decision utility (E4112 closed, results pending ~2027). JNCI 2013;105:701-10
Ernster et al. DCIS detection in screening mammography: ~20% of screen-detected cancers (28.2% at ages 40-49) vs <5% pre-screening - the over-detection debate's founding numbers. JNCI 2002;94:1546-54
AJCC 8th edition: DCIS = Tis; LCIS REMOVED from staging (benign entity); T1mi (<=1 mm) classifies as invasive T1 - the two gates' authority (per NCI PDQ, loaded live)
